back_blocks.md: A **dot and cross diagram** shows the arrangement of outer-shell electrons in an ionic or covalent compound or element, using dots and crosses to represent electrons from different atoms.

cards.back_md: A **dot and cross diagram** shows the arrangement of outer-shell electrons in an ionic or covalent compound or element, using dots and crosses to represent electrons from different atoms.

front_blocks.md: What three conventions must be followed when drawing a dot and cross diagram for an ionic compound?

back_blocks.md:
1. Only **outer-shell electrons** are shown.
2. The ion is enclosed in **square brackets** to show the charge is spread across the whole ion.
3. The **ionic charge** is written at the top right-hand corner outside the brackets.

front_blocks.md: In a covalent dot and cross diagram, all electron shells are shown for each atom.

back_blocks.md: **False.** Only **outer-shell (valence) electrons** are shown in dot and cross diagrams.

front_blocks.md: In a dative covalent bond, **..........**  atom provides **both** electrons. In a displayed formula, this bond is shown by an **..........** pointing away from the lone pair.

back_blocks.md: In a dative covalent bond, **one** atom provides **both** electrons. In a displayed formula, this bond is shown by an **arrow** pointing away from the lone pair.

back_blocks.md: **Coordinate bonding** (also called dative covalent bonding) is a type of covalent bond in which **one atom provides both electrons** needed to form the shared pair.

front_blocks.md: What is the expanded octet rule and which type of element most commonly shows it?

back_blocks.md: The expanded octet rule applies when an atom has **more than eight electrons** in its outer shell. It is most commonly shown by elements in **Period 3 and beyond** (e.g. P, S) that have available d orbitals, such as in PCl<sub>5</sub> and SF<sub>6</sub>.

front_blocks.md: BF<sub>3</sub> obeys the octet rule because boron forms three covalent bonds.

back_blocks.md: **False.** BF<sub>3</sub> is an example of the **incomplete octet rule** — boron has only **six electrons** in its outer shell after forming three bonds, making it electron-deficient.

front_blocks.md: In ionic bonding, metal atoms **..........**  electrons to non-metal atoms. Both ions formed achieve a **..........**  electron configuration.

back_blocks.md: In ionic bonding, metal atoms **transfer** electrons to non-metal atoms. Both ions formed achieve a **noble gas** electron configuration.

front_blocks.md: Describe what is shown by the dot and cross diagram of NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> and identify the type of bonding present.

back_blocks.md: The diagram shows four N–H bonds around a central nitrogen atom, all within square brackets with a 1+ charge. Three bonds are ordinary covalent bonds (one electron from N, one from H) and one is a **dative covalent (coordinate) bond** in which the nitrogen lone pair provides both electrons to bond with H<sup>+</sup>.
